_Most machine learning never makes it to production. Your job is to make sure ours does. We are looking for an ML Engineer who turns models into reliable, maintained systems that construction companies actually use to make better decisions about their equipment and operations. You will work at the intersection of data science and software engineering, shaping how machine learning gets built, deployed, and improved at Trackunit.

**What’s in it for you?

Bring machine learning into everyday use. Turn models and experiments into reliable products that help customers make better decisions about their equipment and operations.

Shape how we build and run ML. Influence the tools, engineering practices, and deployment patterns that take solutions from an initial idea through to production and continuous improvement.

Work on interesting data challenges. Explore how equipment, sensor, and contextual data can support useful predictions and insights for the construction industry.

Build alongside people with different strengths. Collaborate with data scientists, data engineers, and product teams, combining scientific thinking with practical software engineering and customer understanding.

Develop your craft and your career. Join an international environment with knowledge sharing, feedback, and support for your personal and professional development.

**Who are you ideally?

**

• You have MLOps experience taking machine learning solutions into production and maintaining them beyond their initial release.

• You bring strong Python skills and solid software engineering practices, including testing, version control, code reviews, and CI/CD.

• Databricks expertise is a significant advantage.

• You ideally bring strong hands-on experience building ML workflows in Databricks, tracking experiments and managing models with MLflow, and deploying and monitoring models in production.

• You understand the ML lifecycle, from feature preparation and reproducible training to evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and retraining.

• You can work with data scientists to assess model performance, recognise issues such as data leakage and drift, and translate experimental code into maintainable systems.

• You have experience with cloud platforms and tools for orchestrating ML workflows and serving predictions. You can make sensible trade-offs between reliability, performance, and cost.

• You enjoy shaping solutions with others, explaining technical choices clearly, and connecting engineering decisions to customer needs.

• Experience training, tuning, and validating machine learning or deep learning models would be a plus.

• Experience with time series, sensor or geospatial data, or distributed processing would be a plus.

You don’t need experience with every tool or data type listed. If you bring strong engineering skills and enjoy making machine learning useful in practice, we’d like to hear from you.

**Our hiring process

****Don't waste your time on writing the best possible cover letter for the job. We want you to create an impact that matters, and that's not in the cover letter.

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with the Talent Acquisition Partner.

• A deeper conversation: We'll go into your experience and how you work, and you'll get a clearer picture of the team, the challenges, and what the role actually looks like day to day.

• Assignment-specific interview. We want you to get an insight into some of the concrete work tasks or projects related to the role. You will be given a case to prepare prior to the interview, and at the interview, you will present the case to relevant colleagues from across Trackunit, who you’ll also work closely with in the job.

• If needed, throughout the process we will obtain references from former employers and do background checks for level specific, if you have not provided these yourself.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We’re lucky to have you!

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

****We’re committed to construction - one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products – it’s a way of life at Trackunit. We’re proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

Are you passionate about building strong quality systems and helping scientific teams deliver reliable, compliant research? Then Minerva Imaging might be your new place of work!

About the job

Minerva Imaging is seeking an experienced and solution-oriented Quality Assurance Manager to lead and continuously improve the Quality Management System for our Contract Research Organization activities. As a non-GLP CRO, we believe quality should support the business and our clients.

As Quality Assurance Manager, you will serve as an independent quality function and collaborate closely with the Quality Working Group and teams across the organization. You will bring a pragmatic, risk-based approach to quality, challenging existing processes where appropriate and developing solutions that are effective, proportionate, and workable in practice.

About the role

You will own the CRO Quality Management System and ensure that studies and supporting activities are conducted in accordance with company procedures, client requirements, applicable regulations, and recognized quality standards. The role combines strategic development of the quality framework with hands-on management of audits, deviations, CAPAs, document control, training, supplier quality, and study quality oversight.

This position is ideal for someone who is comfortable working independently, enjoys extensive stakeholder management, and can translate quality requirements into clear and effective processes in a dynamic CRO environment. Our quality system is evolving, and we are looking for a pragmatic QA leader who thrives in building quality systems that are both effective and workable. You will be comfortable applying risk-based thinking, focusing effort where it creates the greatest value, and helping the organization strengthen compliance without slowing scientific progress.

The position

As Quality Assurance Manager, you will:

• Own and continuously improve Minerva Imaging's CRO Quality Management System, ensuring practical and risk-based compliance.

• Collaborate with the Quality Group and operational teams to maintain high-quality documentation, effective deviation management, and risk-based decision-making across the organization.

• Lead audits, inspections, deviations, CAPAs, and supplier quality activities while maintaining inspection readiness.

• Educate and coach colleagues across the organization to strengthen quality awareness and ownership.

• Serve as the primary quality partner for clients, management, and operational teams, translating quality requirements into fit-for-purpose solutions that support scientific excellence and business objectives.

What will make you successful

You are a collaborative and pragmatic quality professional who:

• Have a strong understanding of Quality Management Systems and apply quality principles with a pragmatic, risk-based mindset.

• Combine auditing, problem-solving, and root cause investigation skills with a focus on practical solutions.

• Work independently, take ownership, and build strong relationships across scientific, operational, and management teams.

• Can influence stakeholders, navigate competing priorities, and translate quality requirements into clear and workable processes.

• Balance structure and compliance with sound judgement, focusing efforts where they create the greatest value.

• Communicate confidently in English and actively promote a culture of quality, learning, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

• A degree in life sciences, veterinary medicine, pharmacy, biomedical sciences, biotechnology, quality management, or a related field.

• Experience from a CRO, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or research environment.

• Demonstrated experience with quality systems, audits, deviations, CAPAs, root cause investigations, and regulatory compliance.

• Experience implementing or maintaining electronic quality systems is preferred.

• Experience supporting client audits and inspections is highly desirable.

• Formal training in Quality Assurance or Quality Management is preferred.

• Excellent organizational, project management, and stakeholder communication skills.

Minerva offers:

We believe in creating an agile working environment, so we have flexible working options including the option of working from home. We care about our employees’ well-being and offer health insurance and a quality conscious lunch scheme and monthly social activities.

We are an informal organization with a strong focus on open and honest communication. We value humour and a natural care for one another.

Application:

Please submit your application to us no later than 08.11.2026. The application must include a motivated cover letter and a CV addressing the listed qualifications. Applications will be evaluated continuously.

If you have questions regarding the position, please contact Kujtim Rexha, HR Business Partner at kur@minervaimaging.com

About Minerva Imaging:

Minerva Imaging is a scientifically driven and fully integrated Contract Research Organization (CRO) and Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing in targeted radionuclide therapies.

We support translational research and drug development through the use of advanced preclinical animal models within oncology and cardiovascular diseases, combined with state-of-the-art in vivo molecular imaging. By working in close partnership with our sponsors, we seek to understand their scientific challenges and jointly identify how our expertise, technologies, and methods can deliver robust and meaningful answers.

Our modern facility in Ølstykke, Denmark offers best-in-class, fully integrated radiopharmaceutical research, development, and manufacturing capabilities - covering the entire value chain from early research to clinical supply.

Backed by Nordic Capital since 2026, Minerva Imaging is executing an ambitious growth strategy aimed at strengthening our position as a market leader within targeted radionuclide therapies. This growth journey offers exciting opportunities for individuals who want to contribute to cutting-edge science in a dynamic and international environment.

Minerva Imaging is an equal opportunity employer, and we welcome applications from qualified candidates regardless of background or experience. In accordance with our recruitment policy, all candidates are required to provide a personal criminal record as part of the hiring process.

Follow us on LinkedIn for the latest news updates or visit www.minervaimaging.com for more information.

What you’ll do

•

•

•

Who we’re looking for

You’re likely studying marketing, business, communications or a related field. Most importantly, you’re interested in digital marketing and motivated to put that interest into practice.

We imagine that you:

Have a structured approach and enjoy keeping track of details, tasks and deadlines.

• 
Are comfortable working with numbers and curious about why performance changes.

• 
Have a basic working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets.

• 
Take initiative, follow through and ask questions when something is unclear.

• 
Have a commercial mindset and want to understand how advertising contributes to business results.

• 
Communicate clearly in English; a Nordic language is a plus.

• 
Are curious about AI and open to learning new tools.

Ideally, you’ve already had some exposure to advertising platforms, campaign setup or performance reporting. Experience is a plus, but not a requirement if you bring a structured approach, curiosity and a strong motivation to learn.

What we offer

• 
Structured onboarding and hands-on training in advertising platforms.

• 
Close mentorship and regular feedback from our Growth Lead.

• 
Experience working with live campaigns across multiple European markets.

• 
Collaboration with in-house creatives and other marketing specialists.

• 
Growing responsibility as you develop your skills.

• 
A collaborative environment where your ideas and observations are welcome.

Practical information

Hours: Approximately 16-24 hours per week, with the schedule agreed around your studies.

jobs.description:
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

For every Child, the right to Health

Job organizational context:

The Global Transport & Logistics Center (GTLC) within the UNICEF Supply Division in Copenhagen is accountable for securing adequate service provision to deliver development and emergency supplies from vendors or UNICEF hubs to all UNICEF COs and Partners and for the ability to go beyond the port of entry up to the last mile.

This is possible through establishing a five-year intermodal transport contract with global freight forwarders and MOUs with leading carriers. This strategy also aims to support and streamline processes and systems for efficient and timely international transport services and, delivery solutions for UNICEF COs and Partners to secure an end-to-end sustainable supply chain for all countries where UNICEF is present.

In line with the systems strengthening strategy, UNICEF is collaborating with the Global and address bottlenecks in the importation of critical supplies for children, such as vaccines, auxiliary supplies and cold chain equipment; medicines and medical devices; sanitation equipment; and implement appropriate country level process improvement initiatives.

How can you make a difference?

Under the supervision of the GTLC Logistics Manager, the Project Manager will support the ongoing implementation of the ADEPT Programme in existing and additional countries by improving and building systems that enable faster importation, including fiscal and regulatory processes, and clearance of health products, vaccines, and other commodities. The role will also support global policy engagement, importation process improvement initiatives, and stronger public-private collaboration at global and country levels to ensure the timely, efficient, and cost-effective delivery of essential goods to children and vulnerable communities.

• The Project Manager will engage UNICEF offices in mutually agreed countries to support in-country project delivery, as required, by:

• Validating and establishing in-country information and relevant contacts during the initial project validation phase.

• Liaising with relevant stakeholders, including ministries of health and other government agencies, to obtain and maintain support for project activities and working-level collaboration.

• Supporting diagnostic work to map importation processes, including tax exemptions, regulatory approvals, and other clearance requirements.

• Establishing and sourcing the data needed to measure baseline performance and project impact, including time and cost indicators.

• Participating in project governance structures, workshops, and convenings based on diagnostic missions and agreed implementation needs.

• When on mission the Project Manager will collaborate with GATF counterparts on below work assignment overview:

• Convene workshops/joint activities to coordinate the streamlining of the country’s importation processes and procedures and advocate for a single window.

• Enhancing the understanding of each country specificity on importation processes and Customs Clearance requirements to reduce NTBs (non-tariffs barriers) through evidence creation and awareness raising activities.

• Clarify with government the mechanism of financial disbursement between governments agencies and how it affects the importation processes and timelines.

• Establish, in collaboration with the Alliance, the in-country working group overseeing the project implementation as required and participate as needed in public-private working groups in-country to ensure project sustainability.

• Raise awareness of key stakeholders (Government, Humanitarian and Private Sector) on the benefit of GATF’s initiative in digitalization of the importation processes.

• Strengthening related partnerships

• Identify key stakeholders that could be strong partners to lobby or collaborate on related activities.

If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Download File JD Programme_Manager.pdf

_**

UNICEF's Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

UNICEF competencies required for this post are…

(1) Builds and maintains partnerships

(2) Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness

(4) Innovates and embraces change

Familiarize yourself with our competency framework and its different levels.

UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status.

UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence. We offer a wide range of benefits to our staff, including paid parental leave, breastfeeding breaks and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities. UNICEF provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process. If you require any accommodation, please submit your request through the accessibility email button on the UNICEF Careers webpage Accessibility | UNICEF. Should you be shortlisted, please get in touch with the recruiter directly to share further details, enabling us to make the necessary arrangements in advance.

UNICEF does not hire candidates who are married to children (persons under 18). UNICEF has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNICEF, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, fraud, corruption and other forms of serious misconduct.

UNICEF is committed to promoting the protection and safeguarding of all children. All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference, safeguarding and background verification checks. These checks may include verification of academic credentials and employment history, screening against relevant United Nations misconduct databases, and requests for misconduct disclosures from current and former employers, professional associations, other relevant organizations and participating organizations under inter-agency safeguarding initiatives, including the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), where applicable.

Appointment, selection and continued engagement are subject to the satisfactory completion of all required checks. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information and consent to enable UNICEF to undertake these checks .Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s) and employment history. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check, and selected candidates with disabilities may be requested to submit supporting documentation in relation to their disability confidentially.

UNICEF appointments are subject to medical clearance. Issuance of a visa by the host country of the duty station is required for IP positions and will be facilitated by UNICEF. Appointments are conditional on the selected candidates' willingness to comply with current or future vaccination requirements, should UNICEF mandate it for personnel. Failure to comply with such requirements, where applicable and without a duly approved medical exemption from the relevant UN authority, will result in the cancellation of the selection or may lead to other administrative measures, including separation from service.

Remarks:

As per Article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity.

UNICEF is committed to fostering an inclusive, representative, and welcoming workforce. For this position, eligible and suitable male candidates are encouraged to apply.

Government employees who are considered for employment with UNICEF are normally required to resign from their government positions before taking up an assignment with UNICEF. UNICEF reserves the right to withdraw an offer of appointment, without compensation, if a visa or medical clearance is not obtained, or necessary inoculation requirements are not met, within a reasonable period for any reason.

UNICEF does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). UNICEF will not ask for applicants' bank account information.

Mobility is a condition of international professional employment with UNICEF and an underlying premise of the international civil service.

Humanitarian action is a cross-cutting priority within UNICEF's Strategic Plan. UNICEF is committed to stay and deliver in humanitarian contexts. Therefore, all staff, at all levels across all functional areas, can be called upon to be deployed to support humanitarian response, contributing to both strengthening resilience of communities and capacity of national authorities.

All UNICEF positions are advertised, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and advance to the next stage of the selection process. An internal candidate performing at the level of the post in the relevant functional area, or an internal/external candidate in the corresponding Talent Group, may be selected, if suitable for the post, without assessment of other candidates.

Description

Shape the future of Global Benefits Management across the Nordics – building on a strong client portfolio, accelerating growth, raising our market profile and developing the next generation of Nordic GBM talent.

The Role

Lead WTW’s Nordic Global Benefits Management business within Integrated & Global Solutions. This high-impact role combines market leadership, business development, client management and people leadership across Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. As a visible senior representative of WTW, you will build trusted relationships with executive decision-makers and help multinational organisations turn global benefits strategies into action.

This is a market-facing growth role. You will originate, shape and convert significant GBM opportunities across the Nordic region while protecting and expanding WTW’s existing client portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Shape the market – Be a recognised voice for GBM across the Nordics and strengthen WTW’s profile with multinational employers, external advisers and internal stakeholders.

• 
Accelerate growth – Build and convert a sustainable, multi-year Nordic pipeline, winning significant new GBM mandates and creating a stronger platform for long-term growth.

Qualifications

What we offer

Join a collaborative international team with a strong client portfolio and significant room to grow. You will have the platform to shape WTW’s Nordic GBM strategy, build a high-performing regional business and make a visible contribution to our ambitions. We offer flexible working arrangements and a competitive total rewards package, including performance-related and locally relevant benefits.

About WTW and IGS

WTW combines data, insight and expertise to create solutions across people, risk and capital.

You will join WTW’s Integrated & Global Solutions (IGS) team and be based in the Copenhagen or Stockholm area, with flexibility around location.

IGS brings together more than 350 colleagues across WTW’s global network to address the headquarters needs of multinational clients. We help organisations navigate the business, cultural, linguistic and regulatory complexities of operating across markets.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Are you ambitious, skilled at engaging with businesses, motivated by the prospect of achieving measurable sales results and the opportunity to shape your own success?

About Siite

Siite ApS is a full-service web and marketing agency that helps Danish SMEs with digital solutions that drive visibility, growth and measurable business results. We have a team of more than 35 colleagues and work across our departments in sales, web development, marketing and consultancy.

We are currently looking for an ambitious Account Manager in Aalborg who is motivated by delivering results, building strong client relationships and developing their skills within a company with high ambitions.

Briefly about the role

At Siite, you’re an Account Manager.

This means that your responsibility does not end once the agreement has been signed. You will support the client throughout the entire partnership and act as their commercial sparring partner, getting to know their business, monitoring its development and ensuring that we continue to create value. You are responsible for the entire customer journey – from the initial contact and needs assessment through to advising the client, concluding the agreement, following up and developing the customer relationship.

You will be working both to attract new clients and to develop your existing client portfolio. You will take the initiative in establishing new relationships and identifying business opportunities, whilst our in-house appointment bookers will regularly arrange high-quality meetings for you.

Your day-to-day work will involve a mix of proactive sales activities, client meetings, follow-ups and providing ongoing advice to your own client portfolio. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

   

  Further information on the Department at https://nbi.ku.dk/english/. Informal inquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The positions are for three years, starting as soon as possible, with flexible start dates into 2027.

jobs.occupation: Fully funded PhD position in Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies
jobs.description:
The Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies in the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a full-time three-year PhD scholarship, with an expected starting date of 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The PhD project will be part of the research project Sensing Korea: Reframing Korean Studies in the Nordic Countries, funded by the Academy of Korean Studies. Sensing Korea aims to develop sensory and narrative approaches to Korean Studies in order to explore the diversity of Korean experiences beyond essentializing representations.

  The PhD scholarship is funded through the Core University Program for Korean Studies of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Korea and the Korean Studies Promotion Service at the Academy of Korean Studies (AKS-2026-OLU-2250001). Sensing Korea is led by Barbara Wall and hosted by Korean Studies at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, University of Copenhagen. The project runs for five years, from June 2026 to May 2031.

  The PhD candidate will be supervised by project leader Barbara Wall and will work closely with a project team comprising scholars based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies as well as researchers from Korean Studies programs at other Nordic universities. The candidate is also expected to have an interest in communicating academic knowledge about Korea to a broader public.

  About the department
 The project is based at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, which is part of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. The department has approximately 800 students and 150 employees. At the department, we research and teach in language, culture, religion and society, primarily with a focus on regions outside Western Europe and the USA. The work is rooted in language-based area studies and cross-cultural perspectives that provide insight into global contexts and cultural complexity.

  Introduction to the PhD programme
 PhD studies consist of research programmes that qualify students for independent and wide-ranging research, development and teaching at international level. The main emphasis is on PhD students organising and conducting their own research project (under supervision). The programme culminates in the submission of a PhD thesis, which the student must defend in public. The programme is prescribed to 180 ECTS points, corresponding to three years of full-time study. The PhD will have to teach and carry out other tasks at the department as part of the PhD position corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months).

  A PhD opens up a range of career opportunities in academia and elsewhere. As well as writing a thesis, PhD students work in active research environments in Denmark and abroad. They contribute to the academic environment, take research training courses and convey the results of their research in teaching, at academic conferences and to the general public. 

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to a master’s degree in Korean Studies or a related field in the humanities. Particularly relevant disciplinary backgrounds and research interests include Literary Studies and Sensory Studies, as well as Musicology, Media Studies, Religious Studies, Cultural Studies, History, Art History/Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and East Asian Studies. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Korean Studies or a related humanities discipline, with research interests in Literary Studies and/or Sensory Studies, or in another relevant field with a clear connection to sensory and narrative approaches to Korea. Excellent proficiency in Korean and English is essential. Proficiency in a Scandinavian language and/or Literary Sinitic (Hanmun) is considered an advantage.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we will obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency. Applicants must possess skills in written and spoken academic English at a high level. Additional language skills and knowledge of related regions is an advantage. If deemed necessary, the department may request that applicants document their English or other language skills.

  Application
 All applications must be submitted online, in PDF or Microsoft Word format, via the link “Apply for the position” at the bottom of the page. 

  The application must include: 

  Personal statement (max. one page)
 In their personal statements, applicants are encouraged to: 

   	
• outline how the PhD project relates to other research activities at the department, particularly the Sensing Korea project.  	
• describe as clearly as possible their competencies and personal qualifications relevant to the PhD programme and the Sensing Korea project.   CV
 Applications must be accompanied by a CV (max.one page) and a list of publications, where relevant. 

  Documentation (diplomas and transcripts) 
 Applicants must upload the following:

   	
• A copy of their Master’s degree diploma or similar (if this is not available by the application deadline, applicants must document pre-approval of their Master’s thesis) 	
• A copy of their Master’s degree transcript 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree diploma 	
• A copy of their Bachelor’s degree transcript.   Applicants with a degree from a university where the working language is not English or one of the Scandinavian languages must submit a translation of their Master’s diploma and/or diploma transcripts approved by the issuing university of by another local authority. These documents must be translated into English, Danish, Norwegian or Swedish. An official description of the grading scale (and a diploma supplement where relevant) must also be attached. 

  Chinese applicants must attach a China Credentials Verification (CHSI) certificate. Read more about CHSI here: https://www.chsi.com.cn/xlcx/en/index.jsp.

  Project description 
 Applications must include a preliminary project description covering the problem formulation, overall objectives, methodology, design and timetable (max. five pages/12,000 characters, incl. spaces, excl. bibliography). The project description should also give a preliminary indication of what research literature the candidate would expect to engage with. 
 
 On the website of the PhD School, you can find more information about the attachments your need to include with your application:PhD at the Faculty of Humanities – University of Copenhagen / https://phd.humanities.ku.dk/how-to-obtain-a-phd-scholarship/admission-requirements/ .

  Please do not upload or submit recommendations, publications, theses, etc. 

  Assessment criteria
 The following criteria are applied when assessing PhD applications:

   	
• The quality, originality and feasibility of the PhD project and its relevance to the Sensing Korea project 	
• Research qualifications, as reflected in the attached CV and project description  	
• Competencies and knowledge of relevant fields of academic research 	
• Level (grades obtained) of Bachelor and Master’s studies.    Please note that only one position is available and competition is intense. 

  The recruitment process 
 After the deadline for applications, the Head of Department considers advice from the Appointment Committee and then selects applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether or not they have been shortlisted. After this, the Head of Department sets up an expert Assessment Committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Individual applicants will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Enrolment 
 It is a prerequisite for employment that successful applicants enrol at the PhD School of the Faculty of Humanities at the University of Copenhagen. 
 For further information about the structure of the PhD programme, please refer to: Structure of the PhD programme – University of Copenhagen
 For further information about the guidelines for PhD studies at UCPH, please refer to: https://phd.ku.dk/english/

  Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).
 The salary range starts at approximately DKK 30,200 (EUR 4.040) + an 18.07 % pension contribution. According to the agreement, the PhD student is required to carry out tasks at the relevant department to an extent corresponding to 840 working hours (6 months). These tasks are primarily expected to consist of teaching in the department’s study programmes.

  You can read more about employment as a PhD Fellow here: Employment as a PhD student – University of Copenhagen.

  International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk).

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in research, please visit: HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen.

  For further information about the application procedure, please refer to the University of Copenhagen website: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Contact Information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR South at: hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2541/26-2H.

  If you have any questions about the academic content of the PhD programme, please e-mail the PhD coordinator at the Department of Cross-Cultural and Regional Studies, Simon Stjernholm, stjernholm@hum.ku.dk.
 If you have questions related to the Sensing Korea project, please email PI Barbara Wall, barbara.wall@hum.ku.dk
 
 The deadline for applications is 5 November 2026 at 23:59 (CET).
 Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.
